title: Mid-sprint price band trigger & HC cooling playbook
content:
Purpose:
A pragmatic, operational playbook and compact modelling sheet to guide mid-sprint decisions when token demand, price elasticity, or committed capacity diverge from plan. Designed for finance + ops + ENG leads to make consistent hiring / contractor / pricing moves with minimal exec coordination.

Scope and timeframe:
- Time horizon: next 12 months (rolling 4-week and 12-week trigger windows)
- Currency: USD
- Applies to hosted API and Dedicated revenue lines; notes where Private has different thresholds

Key assumptions (input knobs):
- Baseline monthly token consumption growth: +6% MoM
- Base price per 1k tokens (weighted blended): $0.045
- Price elasticity (conservative): -0.5 (i.e., +10% price => -5% volume)
- Gross margin sensitivity to price changes: 60% variable contribution on hosted, 40% on Dedicated (higher fixed infra)
- Average ramp time for hiring IC engineers: 10 weeks to meaningful contribution; contractors: 2–4 weeks
- Reserve burst capacity cost: $0.08 per 1k tokens consumed when used

Scenario summary table (illustrative numbers, update with live metrics):
- Baseline: demand +6% MoM, price = base, hiring cadence unchanged
- Downside (D): demand -25% vs plan over 6 weeks
- Slow-growth (S): demand +1–2% MoM; utilization below forecast 8 weeks
- Surge (U): demand +40% vs plan for 3 consecutive weeks

Quick sensitivity matrix (example outputs for a $10M ARR baseline):
- Price -10% => volume +5% (elasticity -0.5) => revenue roughly -6% => headcount delta: none if margin stays > target; watch contractor run-rate
- Price +10% => volume -5% => revenue roughly +4% => opportunity to defer hiring by 1 cycle and fund 1 senior contractor in support
- Demand -25% (Downside) => revenue -25% => immediate 12–16% reduction to variable spend target required to keep runway steady; consider hiring pause and contractor pullback

Headcount phasing & prioritized role list (order of protection):
1) Customer-facing SRE / Escalation engineers (protect 40% of hires)
2) Platform reliability and runtime engineers (protect 30%)
3) Small features / product teams (deferable 20%)
4) Growth/marketing spend tied to acquisitions (deferable 10%)

Hiring adjustment rules (actionable triggers):
- Trigger A (Immediate hiring freeze): 4-week rolling revenue vs plan <= -12% OR committed capacity utilization < 55% for 3 consecutive weeks.
  Action: freeze external reqs except critical SRE/security; pause onboarding of non-critical contractors; review redeployment of 2-week ramp staff. CFO + VP Eng to approve exceptions within 48 hours.

- Trigger B (Selective slow-down): 8-week rolling revenue vs plan between -6% and -12% OR token yield per USD < plan by 10%
  Action: stop non-essential IC backfills; delay one product hiring cycle; accelerate contractor vs full-time tradeoffs for short-term capacity. Ops to reprice burst capacity and pause new Dedicated capacity sales discounting for 6 weeks.

- Trigger C (Surge protective actions): 3-week demand > +30% vs plan
  Action: immediate burst reserve expansion + short-term contractor pool increase; enable higher price band for new customers in risk segments; evaluate rapid capacity procurement (purchase order window: 10 business days) and canary upward scaling for Dedicated pools.

- Trigger D (Pricing test window): If price change experiment results in revenue delta > +/- 6% after 2 full weeks and elastic response differs from model by >0.2 elasticity points
  Action: pause rollout; finance to run a fast micro-run (1 week) with alternative incentive (credit) and return to previous price if negative impact persists. Flag to Revenue Ops for 24h decision.

Example headcount action table (numeric example anchored to $10M ARR baseline):
- Downside (-25% demand) immediate plan: pause 60% of open reqs, sunset 3 contractor FTE equivalents (C-FTE), redeploy two mid-level ICs to cost-saving project, net FTE reduction (hiring stop + attrition) target over 12 weeks: -8 FTE equivalent labor cost (~$1.2M annual run-rate).
- Slow-growth: pause non-critical hiring; convert 2 planned hires to contractor trial (6 months).
- Surge: accelerate hiring for SRE + infra: +3 contractor FTEs immediate, open 2 expedited reqs for site reliability (marked P0).

Pricing sensitivity quick calc (spreadsheet inputs to maintain):
- Inputs: baseline tokens/month, price per 1k, elasticity, variable cost per 1k, committed capacity fixed cost/month
- Outputs: revenue delta, margin delta, runway weeks saved/lost, headcount funding delta
(attach live model in Confluence or linked notebook for exact numbers)

Runbook: who does what (24–72h cadence)
- Day 0 (trigger detected): Finance runs live sensitivity with current product mix (2h), Ops calculates capacity and burst-cost exposure (2h), Eng triage meets for blocking decisions (4h).
- Day 1: Exec decision meeting (CFO, VP Eng, Head of Revenue Ops) to declare an action tier; comms plan drafted for internal teams and top 5 customers if relevant.
- Day 3–7: Implement freeze/scale actions; monitor KPIs daily (token consumption, ARR per token, committed utilization).

Comms checklist (internal):
- All-hands note draft for impacted teams; one-pager for execs describing financial impact and intended mitigations.
- Customer comms template for Dedicated customers if capacity constraints or price band changes affect SLAs.

Follow-ups and hygiene:
- Weekly review: re-run sensitivity sheet every Monday using last 4 weeks of telemetry; update elasticity estimate quarterly using A/B pricing test results.
- Post-mortem: if action tier was used, produce a short 2-page write-up with delta vs plan and lessons for next cycle.

Appendix: quick calculation examples (fill from live model)
- If baseline tokens/month = 120B tokens, price = $0.045 per 1k tokens, variable cost = $0.018 per 1k tokens, then:
  baseline revenue/month ~ $5.4M; variable cost/month ~ $2.16M; contribution margin ~ 60%
  Downside -25% => revenue ~ $4.05M; contribution falls proportionally; runway impact = (~$1.35M delta) / monthly burn -> X weeks (run live calculation)

Open questions / decisions required:
- Confirm elasticity by route (chat vs embeddings vs fine-tune endpoints) — currently modeled as blended; recommend route-level tagging in billing.
- Define exact committed capacity thaw rules for Dedicated customers (legal input needed).
- Decide default contractor vs hire conversion policy for first half 2026.

Owner and next steps:
- Owner (doc): Aisha Patel (Finance)
- Next step: attach live Google Sheet model, set up weekly finance-ops sync (starting week of 2026-03-08) and validate assumptions with Revenue Ops.

Notes: keep this document short and operational; the live sheet contains the numbers and scenario toggles. Use this as the decision rubric during mid-sprint adjustments.
